title: The "Special-General" Framework Contamination
pattern: Embedding application-specific logic or business rules inside a general-purpose control mechanism.
why_bad: Information leakage. Couples the general framework to a single specific use case, making both components brittle and complex to maintain.
detection: Application-specific constants or endpoints hardcoded inside generic execution engines or routers.
counterexample: A closed application that does not aim to act as a generic library or framework.
fix: Extract application logic into a plugin or hook that implements a generic interface.
source: John Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design*, "Special-General Mixture".
